Former Chez Ma Tante chef de cuisine Gabriel Borges and Five Leaves alum Eric Carney stuck to their Greenpoint neighborhood with 148 Noble Street, named helpfully for its address, in September. Borges is offering a seasonal New American menu with French, Italian, and heavy New Orleans touches (which is where he grew up). Look for oysters with green tomato vinaigrette, Louisiana crab claws in Cajun butter, steak with Swiss chard and turnips, and profiteroles with husk cherries.

Lobster roll pop-up Sailor & Siren opened as a full-on restaurant in early July in Greenpoint. Look for Maine lobster rolls with optional caviar and/or uni, as well as hot dogs sourced from Prospect Butcher Co., dressed with yes, caviar, or blueberry mustard. Desserts are simpler — whoopie pies and pocket pies.

The hit-making team behind Taqueria Ramirez and Carnitas Ramirez — chef Giovanni Cervantes and Tania Apolinar — opened their new soccer bar in Greenpoint in late May. After a busy World Cup season, the bar is slinging beers, tacos, and that Ramirez burger.

blocks.x: Is New York undergoing a Japanese pizza influx? Pizza 4P’s (say it out loud) serves up Japanese Italian dishes and Neapolitan pies with global touches; see: spaghetti with oysters and seaweed, burrata ice cream, and pizza with lotus roots, pork sausage, and hummus or scallops and sweet miso gratin.

blocks.x: Two Texas barbecue superstars teamed up to open a dual-smoked meats joint right in Brooklyn this late August. Barbs B Q’s Chuck Charnichart and Goldee’s Jonny White opened Kirbee’s in Greenpoint, serving plates showcasing their specific points of view when it comes to barbecue. Charnichart takes on a South Texas-meets-Mexican angle with spiced brisket, pork ribs with lime zest, and green spaghetti; White’s approach is more modern, with classic brisket, smoked turkey, and potato salad. Per the way Texas barbecues, Kirbee’s is a casual lunchtime spot, with window ordering and a minimal indoor dining space.

blocks.x: Balera is Williamsburg’s newest pizzeria with two floors, a disco ball, and a menu rooted in the Italian regions of Piedmont and Emilia-Romagna, which opened in April. Look for thin-crust Roman-style pizza, pastas, and a seafood salad chock-full of octopus, shrimp, and potatoes. Per the name, which is Italian for “dance halls,” it’ll have live music or DJs on Friday and Saturday evenings.

While Llama Inn closed in 2025, the team decided to turn the modern Peruvian restaurant into a more casual South American-leaning tavern, which opened in May. Restaurateur Juan Correa and chef Francisco Castillo (their first initials make up the abbreviations in the restaurant name) are now showcasing South American cuisines more broadly, with Peruvian, Chilean, and Argentinian dishes, ingredients, and flavors. Grilled swordfish is served with yellow-eyed beans, and the arroz meloso is very lobster-laden. Drinks include wines from the regions and a special pisco sour.

Chef Jackie Carnesi is leading the kitchen of this breezy raw seafood bar in Williamsburg, which opened in May. Sibling to next-door Cafe Susanne, Bar Susanne serves New York and Northeast-sourced seafood, such as littleneck clam aguachile with passionfruit and hibiscus, pan-cooked whole fish, and brunch service, all in an elegant space with views of the East River and the Williamsburg Bridge.

Top Chef alum Rasika Venkatesa started Mythily, named after her grandmother, as a pop-up that explores Tamil and South Indian cuisines. And now she’s turned it into a restaurant in Williamsburg in September, with a color palette stemming from Kanchipuram saris. Food-wise, look for a scallop crudo with Concord grapes and puli inji, a pickled tamarind-ginger-green chile condiment, and finished with a granita made of jaggery, ginger, and warming spices; Caraflex cabbage that’s slow-roasted with spices and rebuilt layer by layer with sorrel-coconut chutney; and her popular rasmalai-tres leches dessert.

Chef Sirichai Sreparplarn revived his cult-favorite Thai restaurant after a 20-month shutter in Carroll Gardens, relocating to Williamsburg this late August. Ugly Baby 2.0 is now much larger, spread across two floors, with a full liquor license. This means much more room to enjoy his spicy Thai fare, plus cocktails, along with wine and a thoughtful beer list.

Zoli, the new “non-dogmatic seafood restaurant” from Houseman chef Ned Baldwin, is a partnership with Amant founder Lonti Ebers — a Houseman regular who named it after her imaginary dog. In April, GRT Architects converted a former warehouse into a huge space with a restaurant, bar, private dining room, and beautiful rooftop terrace. Anchoring the room is a commission by artist Pierre Huyghe featuring three large choreographed aquariums. On the menu: marinated mussels, surf clams with avocado and serrano peppers, and red shrimp tartare with husk cherries. Also try the bison strip steak or smoked goat sausage.
